about: Physical looks of the board's bodies and display layers: linear-sRGB reflectance (F0 for metals), metallic, perceptual roughness and IOR in Solidcraft's opaque-surface convention; metals store IOR 1.5, which Solidcraft requires and ignores. Sources and the soldermask layer model are in docs/materials.md; est. marks an estimate. The bodies the native model saves look the same for every fabrication; only the mask, finish and legend follow the board's fabrication choices.

laminate.name: FR-4 laminate
laminate.note: Natural FR-4 laminate albedo (est.); silica-filled epoxy and glass-epoxy laminate index 1.55 (handbook values: Palik, CRC). Also the laminate a mask opening leaves bare.

laminate_edge.name: FR-4 laminate edge
laminate_edge.note: The routed edge of the laminate, as the laminate; its weave is the detail.

copper.name: Copper
copper.note: F0 of a board's exposed copper (tracks, pads, vias, fills and the foil lines at the edge): copper in air carries a native Cu2O film a few nanometres thick, so it is not the freshly polished metal (0.955, 0.638, 0.538; Johnson & Christy 1972 via Hoffman's table), whose bright, cool pink read as pale salmon on the board. The film takes the blue down steeply, the green a little and leaves the red: at 440 nm normal reflectance falls from 54 % bare to 10 % under 10 nm of oxide, nearly linearly (about 41 % at 3 nm, from the patent's fit), at 560 nm it stays about 55-65 % under 5 nm, and 630 nm is insensitive to it (Powell, Settles and Kailasam, US 6,525,829 B1, Novellus Systems, 2003: modelled reflectance of Cu under Cu2O). So red keeps the bare value, green takes the middle of that range and blue the 3 nm value; the 3 nm film is est. (a native oxide after days in air). Exposed only when the mask is hidden; under the mask it is covered by the mask cap.

via_bore.name: Shadowed drill
via_bore.note: The inside of a narrow open drill as seen from outside: almost no light returns from a bore five or more diameters deep (est.). The 3D view computes no occlusion, so a plated bore would otherwise light up like an open copper face.

termination.name: Matte tin
termination.note: Tin F0 of plated terminations (est.; the package table's matte tin). Generated bodies take their recorded material's look; this is only the family defaults' stand-in.

solder.name: Reflowed solder
solder.note: Reflowed lead-free SAC solder: the plated tin F0 (est.); it freezes satin, not mirror-bright.

package_body.name: Epoxy mould compound
package_body.note: A placed package's moulded envelope: the package table's epoxy mould compound (est. colour; n from the filler and resin indices, Palik, CRC).

chip_resistor.name: Alumina ceramic
chip_resistor.note: 96 % alumina substrate diffuse reflectance (est. from published 400-700 nm reflectance of thick-film substrates, 0.75-0.85); n from sapphire, n_o = 1.77 (handbook value).

chip_capacitor.name: MLCC ceramic
chip_capacitor.note: Sintered barium-titanate MLCC body, tan (est.); barium titanate is n = 2.4 (Palik, CRC).

overcoat.name: Resistor overcoat
overcoat.note: Glass or epoxy overcoat with a black marking layer (est.).

marking.name: Laser marking
marking.note: A stand-in only (est.): a marking decal takes its finish's cited look.

mask.note: Two-flux soldermask layer with a Saunderson interface correction (docs/materials.md, soldermask layer model). The resin is n = 1.52, so the surface reflects ((1.52-1)/(1.52+1))^2 = 0.043 at normal incidence and its internal diffuse reflectance is 0.60 (first principles; Saunderson's k2). The pigmented body under the lacquer has no interface of its own: the coat reflects at the air boundary, so the body takes IOR 1 and a fully rough, diffuse surface; a mask over copper covers bare copper (Johnson & Christy 1972 via Hoffman's table). Pigments: per-pass transmittance through 20 um (t20) and the light the pigment scatters back over a black base, all est. Red and purple scatter more than green, so copper shows through less (about 1.6x and 1.8x against green's 2.1x); red is a scarlet, not a maroon: most of its colour is pigment scatter. Yellow is a lemon-ochre, mostly scatter, so traces barely lighten it. Black pigment in a resin still scatters a little: a dark grey body (about 2.4 % luminance), never a crushed black. Weave show-through (est.): fully under clear resin, faintly under the translucent pigments, not at all under the opaque ones (black, white, yellow: the pigments needing the most exposure energy). Coat roughness (est. from glossmeter readings: gloss masks 80-94 GU, matte 3-43): clear resin has no pigment to break the surface; the yellow fabricators sell is semi-gloss at best; black matte is the flattest. A glossmeter reads the specular peak through a small aperture; a mask cured over traces, weave and filler is not that flat across a reflected light, so a gloss board shows a light's reflection as a soft sheen, never a mirror image with hard edges. At 0.06 the studio's strip light lay on the board as a crisp-edged white shaft (VM check 13 Nov 2026); 0.16 keeps a clear gloss highlight with soft edges, and the other finishes keep their order above it.
